entry.title: Macro templates, arity, and Style identity

content.markdown:
A Macro has a name, description, source Entry/URL references, tags, an ordered nonempty Style list, and a Macro-level `dynamic_arity`. Each Style has a unique `style_name`, tags and one `template`. A localized template selects a **complete projection atomically**: mode, body, separator and block renderer must come from the same language projection.

Template modes are `text`, `formula_inline`, `formula_display`, and `block`. Fixed placeholders use positional child indices `#0` through `#99`; repeated and omitted references are valid. The arity bound is the highest referenced index plus one, not the number of occurrences. Dynamic templates use `#*` and their separator; that is a Macro contract, not a Style-specific reindexing permission.

Selection order is: explicit selector → retained deprecated runtime `default_style` compatibility → first eligible exact occupied-slot match → original first-Style fallback. An unknown explicit selector is an error. On a no-match fallback, the selected Style remains selected even if it omits supplied children or exposes missing arguments.

Automatic selection compares sets of **filled child indices**, not types, rendered text, visible argument count, or a Lean pattern. Eligibility inspects every locale projection and excludes opaque/custom/block projections from inference; explicit use of those Styles remains valid. Changing language selects a projection inside the same automatically selected Style. Inference never persists `style_name` or mutates children.

The existing Entry `spec.rv.automatic-style-selection-034`, attached directly below this chapter, gives the exact eligibility, escaping, legacy compatibility, and acceptance matrix. It is the detailed contract when a summary here is insufficient.

Consumer-owned output extensions remain opaque. Basics must not guess their slot use, rewrite their program, or specialize selection by Macro name.
